name: Tamar
bio:
Tamar was David's daughter, full sister of Absalom, whose beauty drew the obsessive infatuation of her half-brother Amnon. On the advice of his crafty friend Jonadab, Amnon feigned illness and asked David to send Tamar to prepare food for him by hand. When she brought it to him in his private room, Amnon seized her and demanded she lie with him; Tamar pleaded with him to stop, calling it "a wicked thing" that should not be done in Israel, and urged him instead to ask the king for her in marriage rather than disgrace her — but Amnon, being stronger, overpowered and raped her (2 Samuel 13:1-14). Immediately afterward, his obsession curdled into hatred even greater than his earlier desire, and he had her thrown out and the door bolted behind her. Tamar tore the ornate robe that marked her as a virgin daughter of the king, put ashes on her head, and went away crying aloud; her brother Absalom took her in, telling her to keep silent for now since Amnon was her brother, and Tamar lived on in Absalom's house, "a desolate woman" (2 Samuel 13:15-20).

David was furious when he heard what had happened, but took no action against Amnon; Absalom, for his part, said nothing to Amnon at all, good or bad, while nursing a hatred that would simmer for two full years before erupting in Amnon's murder (2 Samuel 13:21-22, 28-29). Absalom later named his own daughter Tamar after his wronged sister, "a woman of beautiful appearance" in her own right (2 Samuel 14:27).
